To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the simian virus 4 large tumor (T)-antigen sensitizes cells to a p 53-dependent apoptosis pathway, and that two independent T-antigen segments are sufficient to sensitize REF to apoptosis.

(1) the expression of full T antigen, a C-terminal segment (T251-707), or an N-terminal segment of the T antigen (T1-128) sensitized REF to apoptosis induced by 5-FU; (2) the sensitization occurred independently and through a p53-mediated pathway; (3) T251-707 was not targeted to the nucleus; (4) the J domain of T antigen was required for sensitization; and (5) the sensitizing activity
the expression of T antigen in cells renders them sensitive to apoptosis induced by the DNA damaging agent 5-FU.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the regions of SV40 large T antigen that are sufficient to sensitize REF cells to apoptosis.
the ability of T-antigens to sensitize cells expressing these proteins to apoptosis.
the ability of the SV40 T antigen to sensitize cells expressing the T antigen to a p53-mediated apoptotic pathway following genotoxic damage.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the expression of specific T-antigen segments, but not the full-length protein, sensitized cells to apoptosis induced by genotoxic stress, and that this apoptosis was dependent on p53.
T antigen sensitizes cells to apoptosis by a p53-dependent mechanism that is not mediated by p53 transcriptional transactivation.
the expression of SV40 T antigen, either full length or in two independent segments (T1- 127 or T251- 708), is sufficient to sensitize REF and human cells to apoptosis following DNA damage.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the T antigen of SV40 can modulate apoptosis through multiple mechanisms.
T antigen sensitizes cells to apoptosis through at least two independent mechanisms.
T antigen sensitizes cells to apoptosis following genotoxic damage through at least two independent pathways.
The main takeaway from our work is that
T antigen sensitizes cells to 5-fluoro-uracil-induced apoptosis by activating a p53-mediated pathway.
SV40 large T antigen sensitizes cells to apoptosis induced by DNA damage.

the expression of T antigen sensitizes cells to apoptosis in spite of the fact that T antigen is able to inactivate p53, and that this sensitization can occur through at least two independent mechanisms, one involving an N-terminal region and the other involving a C-terminal region.
